 All the broadcast info, latest team news, start times and more as Australia head to Adelaide with a 1-0 lead over England
 Match facts 
 Who: Australia v England
 What: Second ODI in three-match series
 When: November 15, 2026, first ball 2:30pm AEDT (2pm ACDT)
 Where: Adelaide Oval
 Live scores: Match Centre 
 How to watch: Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket

 News and reactions post-play: cricket.com.au and the CA Live app 
 Series fixtures 
 First ODI: Australia won by seven wickets 
 Second ODI: November 15, Adelaide Oval, 2:30pm AEDT (D/N) 
 Third ODI: November 18, Bellerive Oval, Hobart, 2:30pm AEDT (D/N) 
 The squads 
 Australia squad: Mitchell Marsh (c), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Jack Edwards, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Spencer Johnson, Riley Meredith, Ollie Peake, Matthew Renshaw, Liam Scott, Adam Zampa
 Australia's new-look pace attack showed no signs of inexperience in the series opener despite the absence of all-format stars Pat Cummins, Mitch Starc and Josh Hazlewood as they prepare for the upcoming Test series against New Zealand. The 21-year-old Mahli Beardman was outstanding on ODI debut with a six-wicket haul, while new-ball pair Xavier Bartlett (1-46) and Spencer Johnson (3-42) also bowled superbly to roll England for 131 in Perth. With Nathan Ellis, who is recovering from a side strain, still to come back into the side, it's good signs for Australia's fast-bowling depth as they build towards the men's ODI World Cup in October next year. Tasmanian quick Riley Meredith has also been added the squad for the second and third ODIs, travelling to Adelaide from Brisbane on Saturday after playing the first three days of the Tigers' Sheffield Shield loss to Queensland where he took 4-77 in the first innings.
 Mahli, Marsh mayhem leads Aussie romp in wild West 
 Australia's batters didn't have much to do in the series opener after captain Mitch Marsh blasted a 29-ball half-century to kick off the run chase, but No.3 Cooper Connolly , wicketkeeper Josh Inglis and Matthew Renshaw all spent time in the middle.  Cameron Green wasn't required with either bat or ball in the first ODI, while fellow allrounder Liam Scott will be itching for an opportunity in his hometown of Adelaide after  Jack Edwards got the nod at No.7 in Perth.
 Young gun Ollie Peake , only 20 years old but already with eight ODIs to his name, was left on the bench in Perth alongside reserve gloveman Alex Carey , but both could come into contention throughout the series if Australia decide to test out different batting combinations after taking a 1-0 lead.  Travis Head was the only Australian batter dismissed cheaply in the first ODI, bowled for a golden duck when he chopped on for the eighth time in his past 15 international innings.
 England squad: Harry Brook (c), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Eddie Jack, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root
 England's touring party was hit by injury in the lead up to the ODI series with young gun  Ja cob Bethell (knee) and quick Josh Tongue (toe) sent home. Allrounder  James Coles and seamer Eddie Jack , both already part of England's T20 squad, were called up as replacements and joined the side in Perth late Thursday ahead of the series opener.
 Another injury blow for England as young gun sent home 
 Tom Banton and Ben Duckett have been gelling nicely at the top of the order with an average partnership of 71 leading into the series but failed to combat the extra bounce in Perth after dominating on the slower pitches in Pakistan in their previous ODI assignment. All of England's top eight, which includes Joe Root, Harry Brook, wicketkeeper Jordan Cox in the absence of the injured Jos Buttler, Sam Curran, Will Jacks and Liam Dawson were caught behind the wicket in the first ODI, with the quicker and bouncier pitches Down Under set to be a major challenge for the visitors throughout their white-ball tour.
 Left-armer spinner Dawson again got the nod over veteran leggie  Adil Rashid but wasn't required to bowl as Australia reeled in their paltry target within 24 overs. Pace ace Jofra Archer proved a handful at times on his return to the ODI side after being rested for England's tri-series trip to Pakistan, while Gus Atkinson also bowled economically for his 1-40 from 10 overs in Perth and top scored with the bat (29no). England may be tempted to unleash young quick Henry Crocombe in the second ODI after Jamie Overton proved expensive.

 Possible XIs 
 Australia: Mitchell Marsh (c), Travis Head, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Josh Inglis (wk), Matthew Renshaw, Jack Edwards, Xavier Bartlett, Spencer Johnson, Adam Zampa, Mahli Beardman
 England: Tom Banton, Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook (c), Jordan Cox (wk), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Gus Atkinson, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid
 It's hard to see Australia changing a winning formula after such an emphatic victory but they could rotate their quicks especially with Mahli Beardman and Spencer Johnson returning from back injuries at the start of the domestic season in September. South Australian Liam Scott could also come into contention in Adelaide, while Ollie Peake and Alex Carey are the reserve batters if the Aussies decide to switch things up.
 Four allrounders seems like one too many for England but Jacob Bethell's injury has left them light on specialist batters for the series. Rashid Khan, Lloyd Pope and Cameron Boyce are leggies that always fared well for Adelaide Strikers at home in the Big Bash, so could veteran spinner Adil Rashid come into calculations with the longer straight boundaries?

 Form guide 
 Past 10 matches, most recent first. W: win, L: loss, N: no result 
 Australia:  W W L L W W W W L L
 Australia have won just one of their four ODI series in 2026, a 3-0 sweep of Zimbabwe in early September. They are on the cusp of another if they can beat England in Adelaide, which would be a welcome boost for Mitch Marsh's side after 1-2 defeats to Pakistan and Bangladesh in June, and South Africa in late September. Australia will also be out to continue their ODI stranglehold over England having won 11 of the past 14 matches between the two sides.
 England: L W L L L W L W W W
 A heavy loss in the first game against Australia and England's ODI form continues to trend in the wrong direction under coach Brendon McCullum. After starting the 2026 calendar year with a 2-1 series triumph against Sri Lanka in Colombo and 2-1 wins over both India and Sri Lanka again at home, they've now lost four of their past five matches. That includes three straight losses which saw them finish last in a tri-series in Pakistan that also featured Sri Lanka.
 Players to watch 
 Mitch Marsh (Australia): Four ODI half-centuries on the bounce for the red-hot Aussie skipper who is coming off a 29-ball fifty in the series opener that included four massive sixes, with two of those in the same over off Jofra Archer measuring 101 and 113 metres respectively. Marsh produced knocks of 60, 84 and 56 in a three-match series against South Africa in September and although he hasn't kicked on to a three-figure score, he's striking at an impressive 135 runs on average per 100 balls from his seven ODI innings in 2026.

 Marsh belts six-laden fifty in front of hometown crowd 
 Tom Banton (England):  The opener looked in fine touch in Perth with five early boundaries before nicking off to Xavier Bartlett on 25. His partnership with Ben Duckett at the top of the order has been a feature for England in ODIs this year, with the pair averaging 65 for the first wicket in eight innings together. Banton has produced a century and four fifties since coming back into the team in September, averaging 52 and striking at 107 during that period, and will be out to capitalise on his positive start to the tour in Perth.

 Rapid stats
 Australia have won 10 of their past 12 men's ODIs against England including their past three in a row; Australia have won the toss and elected to bowl in each of those past three matches in that span.
 England have lost 15 of their past 18 men's ODIs outside of England; their only three away wins in that span have been against Sri Lanka.
 Australia have won four of their past five men's ODIs in Australia, winning the toss in all five of those matches; they had lost four consecutive games in Australia prior to that span.
 Australia have alternated between wins and losses in their past five men's ODIs at Adelaide Oval, including a six-wicket win over England in that span (November 2022); England have lost seven of their past eight games at the venue.
 Spinners have averaged 68.1 runs per wicket in men's ODIs at Adelaide Oval since the start of 2015, the highest rate of any ground in the world that has hosted at least 10 matches in that span.
 England only scored 131 runs in the opening match of this current series after scoring at least 200 runs in their previous nine matches when batting first; in fact, the last time they scored fewer first innings runs in the format was 110 against India in July 2022.
 Australia have taken at least eight wickets in 11 of their past 12 men's ODIs when bowling first; this has included dismissing the opposition all out in three games in that span.
 Mahli Beardman took 6-24 in the series opener, becoming the first Australian to take a men's ODI five-wicket haul before their 22nd birthday; the previous best performance under that age was when Mitchell Starc took 4-27 against Sri Lanka (November 2010).
 Ben Duckett (England) has scored 479 runs in men's ODIs against Australia, the most against any opponent; prior to the opening match of the current series, he had scored two consecutive centuries against Australia – 107 (September 2024) and 165 (Febraury 2025).
 Spencer Johnson (Australia) has taken multiple wickets in three of his past four men's ODIs; he has taken a total of eight wickets at an average of 23.1 in those games.
